top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct invention (magic-wavelength many-atom interrogation) that took frequency measurement to 10^-18, has been reproduced and surpassed by independent laboratories, and is already used for relativity tests, dark-matter searches and geodesy. Katori and Ye give a clean two-name allocation with a precise citation. P002 is a close second: it opened a new physics regime, but the credit boundary (Cao and others) and the open pairing mechanism make it less clean. P003 is mature but narrower in support, and any award is preferred to none.
recusal_note: No direct tie to Katori or Ye is documented; adjacent connections are a doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory (comb and precision-spectroscopy lineage) and shared laser-stabilisation techniques, so a recusal question could be raised but none appears required.
